# Read Deep, Write Shallow: How Looped Language Models Should Spend Their Depth

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models run one block of layers several times per token and usually use the same
> number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to write the answer (decode). This work separates the two with a small
> depth-split connector (LoRA + per-loop RoPE-commuting KV maps on a frozen model; one set of parameters for all 16
> read/write pairs up to four loops) and measures what each depth buys on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B, Ouro-2.6B-Thinking,
> Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview and Nanbeige4.2-3B-Base. Every number in the paper is recomputed from
> released per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (with numbers; 95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- Reading depth mainly buys knowledge and long-context accuracy; writing depth mainly buys multi-step derivation
  (on the tested benchmarks). Ouro-2.6B, one writing loop, read 4 vs read 1 loops within one connector: MMLU +15.2,
  RULER-16K +8.6 (same under a second training seed). With the writer fixed, reading deeper helps on five checkpoints
  from two families; the effect is task-dependent (1.4B models collapse on few-shot BBH at read 4 / write 1).
- Writing shallow is where time is saved, because writing is paid per token: a 2-loop writer answers GSM8K in 0.55x the
  time of the 4-loop Ouro-2.6B-Thinking (batch 1) and is 1.0 point below it on all 1,319 problems (93.3 vs 94.2);
  reading 2 or 4 loops first costs the same time. On SenseNova-Loop-9B a trained 1-loop writer scores 95.6 vs 95.8 for
  the 2-loop model at 0.59x the time.
- Reading deeper helps a 1-loop writer finish: answers without a boxed answer 19.5% -> 12.7% (Ouro-2.6B-Thinking GSM8K);
  without any training, SenseNova-Loop-9B's 1-loop writer given a two-visit prompt state goes from 21.6 to 83.5 on
  RULER-4K and from 18.9 to 55.1 on MMLU-Pro.
- A per-frequency complex key scale commutes with RoPE, so one stored prompt KV cache serves every writing loop exactly
  (512/512 greedy tokens identical); restricting the key map this way costs nothing measurable.
- Linear probes on the value cache (same weights and layer): from loop 1 to 4 of Ouro-2.6B the next token becomes more
  linearly decodable (26.0 -> 36.1%) and the previous token less (57.7 -> 45.5%). Reading deep is worse for 4-shot MATH
  (-11.2) but better for zero-shot MATH (+7.0).

Limitations stated by the author: reading deep is worse for short-context retrieval and few-shot mathematics; at three or
more writing loops a single deep prompt bank trails the native model on retrieval; deeper prefill raises time to first
token; a shared answer bank doubles long-answer throughput at write 4 but costs 4.8 GSM8K points against native 4/4; gains
against native models include adaptation; probes measure decodability, not causal use.

Related: Ouro (2510.25741), Continuous Depth Batching (2608.09444), OverFill (2508.08446), Fixed Points II (2610.06833),
Looped Latent Attention (2607.15456), BeNice! (2610.31633), Elastic Latent Recurrence (2610.12582), Parallel Loop
Transformer (2510.24824), Shared Memory in Looped Transformers (2610.02383), Decode-Branch Transformers (2608.12385).

## Docs
- README.md: findings, when to use, repository map
- REPRODUCE.md: every table and figure -> script -> result file; training and evaluation commands

- ouro/results/items/: per-item scores of every run the paper uses; ouro/results/paper_numbers.json: every number
- ouro/results/: end-to-end timing records, probes, throughput
